\begin{tablenotes}\footnotesize
\item F1, P, R: element micro-F1, precision and recall against each sample's first coding, design-weighted on the evaluation sample and unweighted on the fresh census; P$-$R: precision minus recall. A failed execution counts as omissions, as registered. Specification \S4m, run on 8 November 2026 on Bedrock EU inference profiles; descriptive, no selection. The three configurations with thinking were re-run under fresh identifiers after a runner defect had stopped their first runs before any run record was written; no figure was computed from those.
\item Requests: Opus 5 (\S4k) and its repeat without temperature and with thinking disabled, the tool forced; Opus 5.5 and the control with the tool chosen freely and adaptive thinking at effort low (Opus 5.5 also at high), which Opus 5.5 requires; Table~\ref{tab:model_config}.
\item (b) Union: an element counts as predicted on a row if any of the three executions predicts it there; intersection: only if all three do. A failed execution predicts nothing, so it empties the intersection and adds nothing to the union for its paragraph (failed executions per run: Opus 5.5, effort low, evaluation sample: 0, 0, 0; Opus 5.5, effort low, census: 0, 0, 0; Opus 5, repeated, evaluation sample: 0, 0, 0; Opus 5, repeated, census: 1, 0, 1). The Opus 5 repeat's first execution against the run of 1 November: element F1 $+0.002$ [$-0.020$, $+0.021$] on the evaluation sample and $-0.022$ [$-0.073$, $+0.028$] on the census.
\item (c) Missed: the number of reference element tuples the first execution does not predict; the shares are design-weighted on the evaluation sample; failed: the paragraph's execution ended without a valid record; row: the record has no row for the reference technology; element: the row exists but lacks the element (Table~\ref{tab:fn_causes}).
\end{tablenotes}
